summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She had been managing at home with TPN, IV fluids, and oral Dilaudid but was not improving. In the hospital, she received IV pain control initially, then transitioned to oral hydromorphone every three hours with good effect. Bowel rest and continued TPN were maintained throughout. She reported persistent constipation, prompting administration of a Fleet’s enema and an enhanced bowel regimen including Miralax and as-needed suppositories. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction or impaction. Her pain and nausea improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition on optimized pain, anti-nausea, and bowel management regimens, with instructions to resume home TPN and follow up with her specialist.
